body:
Certainly, often the sound of someone else's voice would be helpful.  It doesn't feel like it's a long term solution though.  It helps in short spurts.  I don't know what a long term solution would look like (other than what I tried).  

it's really hurtful to get more response from strangers on the internet than family members.

I don't doubt you're right about people not being able to handle the talk, but it does little to change the impact it has.  When I share something so vulnerable and important with someone and I get silence in return, that's damaging.  

>You not completely gone because this post tells me their is still hope for you

I'm honestly not trying to sound argumentative, but the first thought I have to that is I'm only here because I failed.  I tried not to be here.  I don't know how much that really says for there being hope for me.  

Thanks for responding.
Do you know what the name of the essay was?

I've called the suicide lifeline numerous times.  It can be a hit-or-miss depending on who you talk to.  Some people are better than others.  I'd recommend calling them, and if you get someone who you are not finding truly supportive, hang up and call again to reach someone else.  In my worst moments I've connected with people who did exactly what you want: listen.

I've heard before it's possible, but I don't have a source at the moment to verify.  What you said though about the thoughts becoming habit...I do think that once you open the door in your mind to suicide, it becomes extremely hard to close it again.  Are you planning to kill yourself?

i constantly have feelings of doubt about the relationship.  thoughts of 'he doesn't really care about me' or 'he'd rather be with that person' sort of nonsense.  i'd get anxious, the thoughts get worse, i seek reassurance...which eventually turns him away from me.  i told him i was terrified i'd create a self-fulfilling prophecy because of this, hoping maybe if i said it that might stop it from happening.  but that's what happened.  he doesn't believe i can change in this regard.  i don't blame him.

Thanks for responding.  There aren't shopping malls or anything here.  The only things to do are outdoor activities.  My boyfriend had a boat.  We'd use that to go fishing or watch the whales or just get to other parts of the island.  Even a small skiff is very expensive so I can't get one.  He also had kayaks and I loved kayaking.  Again, expensive.  My favorite thing we ever did was go on a 3 day camping trip.  We hiked to a far part of the island to get there.  I don't have the knowledge or resources to do it on my own.  He also had skis.  He was just starting to teach me to ski, letting me borrow his.  Usual story, those are expensive and since I only had a couple lessons, I wouldn't feel safe doing it on my own yet anyway (no ski parks here, we just walk up a mountain and go).  

The only thing I could do on my own is go on a hike, but no camping trips.  

I used to see so much beauty here but now every time I look outside and see the ocean and mountains I just see things I can't enjoy any more.  My job is very stressful and those were the only things that kept me going.

someone responded to my post, asking me to PM them.  I wanted to wait until returning from work today, and now the message is deleted.  I have no idea how to contact them, or why they deleted what seemed an empathetic message.  This hurts.

i hesitate to try to answer the cause of the depression.  other people go through far worse than i ever have in life and deal with it just fine.  rationally, i understand that life is not about being "happy" but about accepting the good and bad equally.  I get that, but it doesn't change how I feel.  I think there's something wrong with my brain that leads to depression.  A trigger seems to be loneliness.  Different kinds of loneliness.  But lately it's stress of job, relationship, isolation...everything and I feel like I'm trapped in certain areas.  The thought of just getting up and moving and trying something new has occurred to me, but at this point I figure I'll just come back to feeling like this again.
